review: S08 independent durability and security review
scope: GitHub issue #31: private body-free save intent and atomic final-file publication

validation.filesystem: Real temporary filesystem with injected write, flush, publication, replay, and update faults

reviewedBehavior: Intent is body-free, checksummed, bounded, and retains private lexical/canonical aliases and normalized metadata.
Intent temp write and fsync precede atomic intent rename; final Markdown temp write and fsync precede atomic no-clobber creation or guarded update rename.
An older valid intent remains readable with its original alias and metadata after a later update, marked superseded and not replayed over newer bytes.
Transient EBUSY intent reads remain retryable without quarantine; invalid and oversized intents are quarantined with stable diagnostics.
Final-file verification uses bounded fstat and chunked hashing; destination parent device is checked against the private root before intent and before final publication.
After publication and without authoritative ACK, final bytes and intent remain, and the private publisher reports enqueue_failed without queued or jobId.
deferredScope: S09 owns authoritative source metadata and job transaction, owner-assigned desiredRevision, ACK, and intent cleanup.
Issue #37 owns public save producer wiring to this private publisher.
documentedLimits: Node path APIs cannot fully exclude adversarial junction retargeting between containment checks and path-based publication; issue #31 records this residual bound.
Windows Node does not portably fsync directory handles; file-handle fsync and same-volume atomic publication are covered, while sudden power-loss directory-entry durability remains a release gate.
